physical_harm: Injuries resulting in death and injuries to the informant, his son and another eye-witness
number_of_offences: Four offences/counts charged; two finally upheld (A2 convicted under Sections 302 and 323, A1 convicted under Section 323)
key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted that the recovery of weapons from A1 and A2 was not proved, and the statements of the prosecution witnesses were contradictory, twisted, and improved, thus not reliable for conviction under Section 302 IPC.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the main witnesses as untrustworthy due to their contradictory statements, twisting of facts, and improvements made, which cast serious doubt on their credibility.
bail_history: Appellant-Mohd. Jamil (A2) is on bail during the pendency of this appeal
trial_duration: Dates of offence: 09.01.1999; Trial judgment: 25.07.2001; High Court decision: 26.10.2009; Supreme Court decision: 12 January 2024
legal_representation: P. N. Puri, Rahul Sharma, Mrs. Reeta Dewan Puri, Ravinder Pratap Singh, Manish Dhingra, Ayush Bhatia, Dr. Monika Gusain, Ashok Mathur, Advs. for the appearing parties
investigation_status: FIR registered on 09.01.1999; charge sheet filed on 01.04.2003; trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court: Conviction of A1 under Section 323, acquittal under Section 302/34; High Court: Acquittal of A1 under Section 302/34 upheld, conviction of A2 under Section 302 and 323 read with s. 34; Supreme Court: Conviction of A2 under Section 302 and 323 read with s. 34 set aside, conviction under Section 323 read with s. 34 maintained
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the conviction of Mohd. Jamil (A2) under Section 302 read with Section 34 IPC is based on unimpeachable evidence and that the High Court ought not to have acquitted Mohd. Yunus (A1) of the charge under Section 302 read with Section 34 IPC.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the FIR is ante-timed and delayed, the conviction is based on the testimony of interested witnesses, and the presence of the informant (PW-1) is doubtful. They also pointed out contradictions and omissions in the statements of the prosecution witnesses.
legal_principle_applied: For trial under Section 302 IPC, if a witness is branded as untrustworthy having allegedly twisted the facts and made contrary statements, it is not safe to impose conviction on the basis of such witness's statement. When there is an effort to falsely implicate one accused person, the statement of such an eyewitness cannot be relied upon without strong corroboration.
sentencing_rationale: The final sentence was imposed because the conviction of Mohd. Jamil (A2) under Section 302 read with Section 34 IPC was set aside due to unreliable witness statements, but his conviction under Section 323 read with Section 34 IPC was maintained.
